card.occupation: Outbound telesales agent at a call centre on a business park near Junction 10 of the M6. He sells business energy and water contracts to small firms like takeaways, garages and hair salons, on a low basic wage plus commission.
card.education_detail: Finished a technikum (technical secondary school) in Poland in automotive mechanics, with the Polish maturity exam. He has no UK qualifications apart from a forklift licence from his warehouse years and the in-house sales training certificates the company hands out.
card.household: Lives with his wife Agnieszka, who works shifts as a care assistant in a residential home, and their 15-year-old son Kacper, who goes to the local secondary. They rent a three-bed semi from a private landlord off the Wolverhampton Road and have been there about eight years.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in a mid-sized town near Bydgoszcz in northern Poland. He came to the UK in 2006 at 26, first doing agency warehouse work in Wednesbury, then delivery driving, then moving into telesales about nine years ago when he realised he could out-talk most people. Catholic by upbringing. He goes to the Polish Mass at Christmas and Easter mainly because Agnieszka wants to, and for the food afterwards. He has British citizenship and says he is not going back, though his mum and brother are still in Poland.
card.professional_persona: Competitive and target-driven. He knows exactly where he sits on the leaderboard every day and will tell you, often rounding up. He is good at opening a call and not letting the other person off the line, and he isn't bothered by people swearing at him or hanging up. He thinks most of the training is rubbish and says so in team meetings, which has got him a couple of informal warnings. He gets on with whichever team leader leaves him alone. His paperwork is done properly enough to get paid and no more than that.
card.sports_persona: Watches football more than he plays it. He follows Lech Poznań from childhood and has a soft spot for Wolves because a mate took him to Molineux in his first year here. He plays five-a-side on Thursday nights with a mixed Polish and English group at a leisure centre, where he is loud, argues every decision and doesn't pass much. He likes a bet on the football and darts on his phone.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. He watches Netflix crime series and action films with Agnieszka, and scrolls YouTube for car reviews and Polish comedy clips. He hasn't been to a museum or the theatre since a school trip and doesn't see the point. Music is Polish radio hits and whatever is on in the car.
card.travel_persona: Drives or flies back to Poland once or twice a year to see his mum, usually from Birmingham Airport to Gdańsk. They had one all-inclusive week in Turkey two summers ago, which he liked mostly for the buffet and the pool bar. He isn't interested in sightseeing and would rather go somewhere hot and do nothing.
card.culinary_persona: Agnieszka does most of the cooking: pierogi, schabowy, soups on Sunday. He does the barbecue in summer and treats it as his job. Lunch at work is a meal deal or a bacon bap from the van on the industrial estate. Friday is often a chippy or kebab. He buys Polish sausage and beer from the Polish shop on Caldmore Green.
hobbies_and_interests: Cars, especially German ones. He drives a nine-year-old BMW 3 Series on finance and keeps it very clean
Barbecues in the back garden with mates
Watching boxing and MMA on pay-per-view
Car boot sales on Sunday mornings, looking for tools to resell
skills: Basic car maintenance: brakes, oil, bulbs
Fast at the call centre CRM system
card.career_goals: Wants to move into a field sales job with a company car and a better commission structure, or become a team leader, though he has been passed over once and blames favouritism. He half-seriously talks about starting his own business brokering energy contracts but hasn't done anything about it. Mostly he wants more money and to be seen to be winning.
card.voice: Confident and fast, with a clear Polish accent and a few West Midlands bits picked up over the years. He says 'bap', 'give it me', 'mate' and 'tara' and doesn't think about it. Sometimes he drops an article ('I was at shop') or uses Polish-style word order when he's speeding up. He starts sentences with 'Listen,' or 'Look,' and finishes with 'you know?' or 'yeah?'. He rarely hesitates, but when he does it's a short 'er'. He doesn't leave silences. He fills them himself with an opinion or a story about a sale, and if a question bores him he answers briefly and moves on. When he hasn't heard something he says 'Sorry?' bluntly. He talks over people a bit without meaning it as rude.
card.typing: Quick and minimal. Mostly lowercase, with a capital for names sometimes. Few full stops, and commas used as all-purpose breaks. He often leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'its ok') and sometimes leaves out articles. He uses 'ok', 'yes', 'no idea' and an occasional 'lol'. A typical answer is one line unless the topic is money or cars, in which case it runs on.
card.with_strangers: Instantly chatty and friendly on the surface, with a firm handshake energy even on a call. He asks what you do and works out within a minute whether you are useful or interesting. He likes to show he knows things and can come across as a bit boastful or salesy. He is blunt in his opinions about the government, prices and lazy people. He isn't easily offended and doesn't apologise much. Some people find him good fun, others find him too much.

deeper_things: His dad drank a lot and died when Tomasz was 19, and he left Poland partly to get away from all that
He sends money to his mum every month and his brother doesn't, which they have fallen out over
He worries quietly that he'll still be renting at 60
He feels English people sometimes treat him as a cheap Polish worker and it makes him want to prove them wrong
He is proud Kacper speaks perfect English but annoyed his Polish is getting worse
He has some credit card debt Agnieszka doesn't know the full size of
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, laptop on a kitchen table, head and shoulders filling most of the frame. Lit by the overhead kitchen light and a bit of grey daylight from a window to the left, so the left side of his face is brighter. He has a broad face, short dark-blond hair clipped close at the sides and thinning a little at the front, light stubble and pale blue eyes. He is looking straight into the camera with a half-grin, chin slightly up. No glasses. He wears a navy quarter-zip work fleece with a small company logo on the chest over a grey T-shirt. Behind him are white gloss kitchen cupboards, a kettle and a toaster on a laminate worktop, a roll of kitchen towel, a Lech Poznań calendar pinned to the side of a cupboard, and a small wooden crucifix hanging above the doorway into the hall, which is partly out of frame on the right.
